title: Finite-time effects in periodically kicked systems
authors: F. Revuelta, R. Chacón, F. Borondo
abstract: In this work, we study finite-time effects in ultracold atomic systems by considering time-dependent modulations with variable waveforms and durations. These two characteristics can be controlled by adjusting only a single parameter. For arbitrarily short pulses, our model recovers the paradigmatic kicked rotor while maintaining the impulse transmitted per period and unit amplitude constant. Furthermore, we demonstrate that finite-time effects have a profound impact on dynamical localization, a result that cannot be captured by the δ-kicked-rotor model. Through a detailed analysis of the effects of different modulation amplitudes, periods, and waveforms, we identify the conditions for which dynamical localization is significantly enhanced. We show that the strength of dynamical localization increases sharply as the system approaches the δ-kicked-rotor limiting case. Moreover, we establish the existence of an optimal value of the period that maximizes dynamical localization for given values of the amplitude and shape parameter.
summary: This paper explores how the finite duration and specific waveform of periodic modulation affect quantum dynamics in ultracold atoms. By analyzing the system's response, the authors demonstrate that these finite-time effects are critical, leading to a measurable enhancement of dynamical localization. The findings establish a pathway to optimize experimental control by identifying optimal modulation periods.
main_problem: The study investigates finite-time effects in periodically kicked quantum systems, specifically analyzing how these effects modify dynamical localization (DL).
main_result: Finite-time effects are crucial, as they significantly enhance dynamical localization beyond what the standard delta-kicked-rotor model predicts, and an optimal modulation period exists to maximize this enhancement.
method: The authors analyze the system by varying the modulation waveform and duration using a shape parameter, comparing quantum and classical momentum dispersions.
model_or_system: The system models ultracold atomic gases in an optical lattice subjected to time-dependent modulation, described by a Hamiltonian involving Jacobi elliptic functions.
key_observables: Dynamical Localization (DL), the difference between classical and quantum momentum dispersion ($\Delta p_{C-Q}$), and the chaotic layer width.
important_parameters: Modulation amplitude ($F$), period ($	ilde{T}$), and the shape parameter ($m$), which controls the waveform from static to pulsed.
main_assumptions: The model maintains a constant transmitted impulse per period while varying the waveform via the shape parameter $m$.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the time series of the modulation function for different $m$ values, and show the dependence of the chaotic layer width and $\Delta p_{C-Q}$ on parameters like $F$, $m$, and $T$.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the model using a time-dependent Hamiltonian, analyzes the impact of the shape parameter $m$ to transition between integrable and kicked regimes, and then quantitatively compares quantum and classical dynamics to map out the conditions for enhanced DL.
why_interesting: This work directly addresses non-adiabatic effects in periodically driven quantum systems, which is highly relevant for controlling quantum dynamics in cold atom experiments and quantum simulation platforms.
